text:
lena-cs: Heads up — ACME reported a ~70% drop in vectors/sec on the embeddings endpoint (embed-v2) after the 03/15 deploy. tokens/sec looks stable, but customers see higher latency and intermittent 504s. cc @aj @raman

aj: on it. Do we have a sample request id?

lena-cs: sample request id `req_20260315_9f3b` from their tenant. They say vector dim looks same in payload but throughput per-second is down. No obvious client-side changes.

raman: quick hypothesis: model variant fallback or quantized/fast path got routed more often -> smaller batched efficiency. Can someone grab model routing logs + batch sizes for that tenant?

jen-sre: looking at infra metrics now — GPU queue depth for the dedicated pool jumped from p50=1 to p95=9 around 15:22 UTC. GPU util ~94% at the same time. I see increased `batch_window_ms` occuring (more immediate publishes, smaller effective batch sizes).

maria: any dim mismatch errors in API logs? Sometimes we log `vector_dim_mismatch` when fallback occurs.

lena-cs: grepping logs: \n```
2026-03-15T15:21:42Z router info tenant=acme model=embed-v2 selected=embed-v2-quant reason=fastpath
2026-03-15T15:21:42Z batcher debug tenant=acme batch_size=2 batch_window_ms=8
2026-03-15T15:21:43Z runtime warn tenant=acme queue_depth=7 gpu_util=94% tokens_in=120 vectors_out=4
```\nNo explicit `vector_dim_mismatch` entries.

raman: nice logs — `batch_size=2` is killer for throughput. If the quant variant has slower per-token exec (or smaller beam) we lose amortization. Also check kvcache hit rate and autoscaler events.

aj: can someone run these quick checks?
- kvcache hit rate for tenant between 15:15-15:30 UTC
- model-variant routing histogram for embed-v2 during the window
- autoscaler replica counts for the dedicated pool

jen-sre: autoscaler shows a slow pickup: min_replicas=3, scaled to 4 at 15:24, to 5 at 15:40. There was a ~3m window where queue depth stayed high before scaling.

maria: kv cache hit rate dropped from 82% -> 21% in that window for the tenant. That explains the increased runtime work per request.

raman: so combined factors: lower kv hits + routing to quant variant + small batch sizes -> higher GPU load and inefficient tokens/vectors amortization. Suggest temporary mitigations: force routing to fp16 variant for that tenant and bump autoscaler min replicas to avoid the slow ramp.

lena-cs: can we try forcing variant? customer open to quick fix.

aj: I'll push a routing override for `tenant=acme` to `embed-v2-fp16` and set autoscaler min_replicas=5 for their pool. Monitor for 20m.

deploy-bot: Deploy triggered by aj: config/overrides/tenant-acme-routing -> embed-v2-fp16 (id: deploy_20260315_1530)

jen-sre: applied autoscaler change (min_replicas=5) at 15:33 UTC.

lena-cs: ACME confirms at 15:44 UTC: vectors/sec back to expected baseline, latency reduced, 504s stopped. :tada:

raman: good fast rollback. Root cause action items:
- investigate why KV cache hit rate dropped (cache eviction/TTL/traffic shift)
- verify quant variant performance profile for small batches and update routing policy to avoid quant for high-latency-sensitive tenants
- tune autoscaler to react faster on queue depth (or add reactive headroom)

aj: logging these actions in the ticket and creating a follow-up runbook. I'll also schedule a short postmortem with ML infra + SRE to decide permanent fix.

lena-cs: thanks all — leaving ticket open until root cause follow-ups.

jen-sre: I’ll collect graphs and a short metric snapshot for the postmortem.

raman: one more reproduce step for engineers: run this synthetic client against the dedicated pool with KV cache disabled to simulate worst-case and measure vectors/sec. Example curl: \n```
curl -sS -X POST "https://inference.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Model-Variant: embed-v2-quant" \
  -d '{"input": "...long document...", "cache": false}'
```\nCollect `batch_size` and `vector_rate` from runtime logs.

maria: adding ticket labels: `impact:high`, `prod:dedicated-pool`, `area:kv-cache`, `area:routing`.

lena-cs: ack. Thanks everyone.
